newsitem.title: USA: Alyeska pump station shutdown decisions pending.
newsitem.headline: Alyeska pump station shutdown decisions pending.

text.p: The operator of the trans-Alaska pipeline will decide in the next two months whether to idle two more pump stations along the 800-mile oil line, the company's president said on Monday.
Bob Malone, president of Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., said declining oil flow through the pipeline may trigger the next in a series of scheduled pump-station shutdowns, likely to occur next year.

"The decision itself will be made over the next 60 days," Malone said at a meeting of the Anchorage Chamber of Commerce. "It's an economic decision. It's simply based on throughput and the cost of operating the pump stations and (drag-reduction agent)."
Shutdowns of some of the system's 12 pump stations were initially scheduled by Alyeska last year and long envisioned as a response to declining North Slope oil production.
Oil flow through the line has declined from a 1988 peak of over 2 million barrels a day to the current 1.4 million barrels a day, reflect declining production at the maturing Prudhoe Bay oilfield.
